title: DNA extraction and genomic sequencing
author: Graham S Sellers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.butanwie
materials: SPRI based DNA extraction Before beginning DNA extraction Thaw samples on ice. Centrifuge 1.5 ml Eppendorf LoBind tube containing nematode sample at ≥ 10,000 xg for 1 min to ensure sample is at bottom of tube. Pipette off excess water if sample is stored in water, be careful not to remove sample. A small volume of water remaining (~10 μl) will not affect extraction. Take DNA Extraction Bead Solution from the fridge and allow it to reach room temperature. Vortex to mix thoroughly prior to use. Create Lysis Master Mix : 730 μl Lysis Solution , 250 μl Tissue Lysis Additive and 60 μl PK . Vortex to mix. Incubate at 55°C until required. Incubate Elution Buffer at 55°C until required. Lysis Add 200 μl Lysis Master Mix to 1.5 ml LoBind tube containing nematode sample. Vortex briefly to mix and centrifuge tube for 1 sec Place in Thermomixer at 55°C for 90 mins at 550 rpm. Centrifuge tube for 1 sec Inhibitor removal Add 70 μl (0.3 X volume) of Flocculant Solution , invert several times to mix and incubate on ice for a minimum of 10 min Centrifuge at ≥ 10,000 xg for 2 min at room temperature Without disturbing the pellet, transfer supernatant to a fresh 1.5 ml LoBind tube SPRI DNA binding Add 400 μl (2 X volume) of DNA Extraction Bead Solution . Place on HulaMixer (continual rotation) for 10 min Place on magnetic stand until supernatant is clear and beads are bound towards magnet While on the stand carefully remove and discard supernatant without disturbing beads Wash Add 1000 μl Wash Solution . Incubate at room temperature for 30 secs While on the stand carefully remove and discard supernatant without disturbing beads Repeat steps 11 to 12 a further time Centrifuge tube for 1 sec. Place back on magnetic stand ensuring beads are bound towards magnet. Remove all remaining Wash Solution with a 10 μl pipette. Air dry tube with cap open until beads are completely dry (i.e. no longer shiny) Elution Add 25 μl Elution Buffer (55°C) and gently flick to resuspend beads. Ensure all beads are resuspended with no clumps. Centrifuge tube for 1 sec Place in Thermomixer at 55°C for 10 mins at 550 rpm. Centrifuge tube for 1 sec Place on magnetic stand until supernatant is clear and beads are bound towards magnet Carefully transfer eluate to a fresh 1.5 ml LoBind tube without disturbing beads Store DNA at -20°C until required.

steps.title: Thaw samples and reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw the DNA samples on ice. Thaw the Rapid PCR Barcoding Kit reagents (Barcodes RLB 01‑12a) at room temperature and keep the Fragmentation Mix (FRM) on ice. Keep all reagents on ice until use, vortex briefly and spin down before use.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Quantify 2 µl of each sample on a Qubit 3.0 fluorometer using the high‑sensitivity (HS) dsDNA assay.

steps.title: Fragment DNA via tagmentation
steps.instruction: If the sample DNA concentration is < 1 ng/µl, use 5 µl of sample; otherwise use 3 µl (maximum 5 ng total). Add the chosen volume to 1 µl FRM in a 0.2 ml PCR tube, flick gently, centrifuge briefly, and place on ice. Run the tube in a thermal cycler: 1 min @ 30 °C, 1 min @ 80 °C, then hold at 4 °C. The DNA is now tagmented; keep on ice until further use.

steps.title: Prepare PCR barcoding master mix
steps.instruction: For each sample prepare a PCR master mix (allow ~5 % excess): 20 µl nuclease‑free water + 25 µl LongAmp Taq 2× master mix. Add 45 µl of this master mix to the tagmented sample and 1 µl of the appropriate Rapid PCR Barcoding (RLB 01‑12a) barcode. Flick gently, centrifuge briefly, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Run PCR barcoding thermal cycle
steps.instruction: If the initial DNA template is > 0.1 ng/µl, program the cycler: 3 min @ 95 °C; 15 cycles of 15 s @ 95 °C, 15 s @ 56 °C, 6 min @ 65 °C; 6 min @ 65 °C; hold at 4 °C. If the template is ≤ 0.1 ng/µl, use 20 cycles of the same cycle. After PCR, store barcoded samples in a refrigerator (4 °C) overnight or up to one week if needed.

steps.title: Bead cleanup and sample concentration
steps.instruction: Perform magnetic bead cleanup to concentrate the library.

substeps.instruction: If the magnetic rack cannot hold 0.2 ml PCR tubes, transfer each PCR‑barcoded sample to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube.
Remove Library Prep Bead Solution from the fridge, let it reach room temperature, and vortex thoroughly.
Create Lysis Master Mix by vortexing together 730 µl Lysis Solution, 250 µl Tissue Lysis Additive, and 60 µl PK; incubate at 55 °C until needed.
Incubate Library Buffer at 55 °C until needed.
Add 50 µl (1×) Library Prep Bead Solution to each sample, pipette‑mix, and let stand at room temperature for 10 min.
Place tubes on a magnetic stand until the supernatant is clear and beads are bound to the magnet.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.
Add 150 µl Wash Solution, incubate 30 s at room temperature, then remove supernatant as before.
Repeat the wash step once more.
Centrifuge the tube for 1 s, return to the magnetic stand, and remove any remaining Wash Solution with a 10 µl pipette.
Air‑dry the tube with the cap open until beads are completely dry (no longer shiny).
Add 15 µl Library Buffer (pre‑warmed to 55 °C), flick to resuspend beads, and ensure no clumps remain.
Centrifuge for 1 s, let stand 10 min at room temperature.
Place on the magnetic stand, then transfer the eluate to a fresh 0.2 ml PCR tube without disturbing the beads.
Store the concentrated samples in a refrigerator (4 °C) overnight or up to one week if required.

steps.title: Quantify concentrated DNA
steps.instruction: Quantify 2 µl of each concentrated sample on a Qubit 3.0 fluorometer using the high‑sensitivity (HS) dsDNA assay.

steps.title: Estimate fragment length
steps.instruction: Choose one of three methods to estimate fragment length: (1) Measure 1 µl of each sample on a Tapestation 2200 (Agilent) with genomic tape (ideal, expensive); (2) Run 2 µl of each sample on a 1 % agarose gel alongside 0.5 µl Generuler 1 Kb DNA ladder (diluted 1:20) (cheaper, less accurate); or (3) Assume a fragment length of 7 Kb for all samples (free, least accurate).

steps.title: Calculate sample molarity
steps.instruction: Calculate molarity (fmol/µl) using: fmol/µl = DNA concentration / ((DNA fragment length × 1,000 × 617.96) + 36.04) × 1,000,000, where DNA concentration is in ng/µl and fragment length in Kb.

steps.title: Pool samples to target concentration
steps.instruction: Pool the samples as equimolarly as possible aiming for a final library concentration of ~2 fmol/µl (5 µl of library for 12 samples yields 5‑10 fmol, ideal for Flongle). If needed, concentrate (repeat step 6) or dilute with Library Buffer to reach the target. After adjustment, quantify 2 µl of the pooled library on a Qubit 3.0 and recalculate molarity using the average fragment length.

steps.title: Ligate sequencing adapters
steps.instruction: Allow the Rapid Adapter (RAP) to reach room temperature, vortex briefly and spin down. Transfer 5 µl of the final library into a 1.5 ml LoBind tube, add 0.5 µl RAP, flick gently, spin down, incubate 5–10 min at room temperature, then place on ice until loading.

steps.title: Load Flongle flow cell
steps.instruction: Perform a flow‑cell quality check as described in the Flongle protocol, then load the prepared library onto the Flongle flow cell following the official ‘Loading the Flongle flow cell’ instructions.

steps.title: Run sequencing run
steps.instruction: Create a dedicated output directory (e.g., on a desktop or external drive) instead of using MinKNOW’s default. In MinKNOW, disable all base‑calling options (base‑calling will be performed later with Guppy GPU HAC). Start the sequencing run for the default 24 hours (longer runs are possible but data typically plateau around 24 h).
